issues.legal_issue: The central revisional authority may grant a mining-lease application through a direction to the state authority to issue the lease.
material_facts: The applicant sought a mining lease, and the state authority did not decide the application despite a direction to do so.
On a later revision, the central authority directed the state authority to grant the lease over a compact block selected by the applicant.
issues.conclusion: The central authority’s direction left the state authority no discretion to reject the application and was, in substance, an order granting the applicant’s request.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 54 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 makes the Central Government a revisional tribunal against orders of the State Government and gives it the same powers as the State Government. The Court relied on State of Assam v. Om Prakash Mehta, which recognised that the revisional authority may pass an order it considers just and proper, including an order granting an application.

predicates.mining_lease_revision_case: A proceeding concerns review of a state authority’s decision or failure to decide an application for a mining lease.
predicates.revisional_authority_has_power_to_grant: The revisional authority has power to make an order granting the application under review.
predicates.central_authority_directed_state_to_gran: The central revisional authority directed the state authority to grant the application.

issues.definition: When a mining-lease revision gives the revisional authority power to grant the application and it directs the state authority to do so, the direction operates as a grant.

issues.legal_issue: A state authority must comply with an unvaried direction of a superior revisional authority and cannot reject the application on its own grounds.
material_facts: The central authority directed the state authority to grant the mining lease over a compact block selected by the applicant.
The state authority later rejected the application, first relying on a policy concerning cement factories and then on pending litigation.
The central authority had not revised or vacated its earlier direction.
issues.conclusion: The state authority was bound to implement the earlier direction and could not refuse to do so unless the central authority itself revised that direction.
issues.legal_principle: A subordinate authority must carry out the orders of the superior revisional tribunal; permitting it to disregard those orders would undermine judicial discipline. If the state authority cannot implement a direction, or a later ground warrants reconsideration, it must refer the matter to the central authority rather than reject the application itself.

rule.if: mining_lease_revision_case and prior_central_grant_direction and state_rejected_application_despite_direction and not central_revised_prior_direction

predicates.mining_lease_revision_case: A proceeding concerns review of a state authority’s decision or failure to decide an application for a mining lease.
predicates.prior_central_grant_direction: The central revisional authority previously directed the state authority to grant the application.
predicates.state_rejected_application_despite_direc: The state authority rejected the application despite the central authority’s direction.
predicates.central_revised_prior_direction: The central authority revised or vacated its earlier direction.

issues.definition: When a central authority has directed a grant, the state authority has rejected the application despite that direction, and the central authority has not changed it, the state authority must implement the direction.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional authority cannot uphold a state authority’s rejection contrary to its earlier unvaried order unless a fresh ground arose after that order.
material_facts: The state authority rejected the application despite the central authority’s earlier direction to grant the lease.
The central authority upheld the rejection in a later revision, relying on litigation concerning the area that had already been pending when it made its earlier direction.
The earlier direction had not been varied or vacated.
issues.conclusion: The central authority had no legal justification to go back on its earlier order because the cited litigation was not a fresh ground arising after that order; it should have set aside the state authority’s rejection and directed implementation of the grant.
issues.legal_principle: Even assuming the central authority could revise its earlier order, it could do so only if a fresh ground arose warranting reconsideration. A ground already known when the earlier order was made does not justify going back on that unvaried and unvacated order.

rule.if: mining_lease_revision_case and prior_central_order_unvaried and later_review_reconsidered_prior_order and not fresh_ground_arose_after_prior_order

predicates.mining_lease_revision_case: A proceeding concerns review of a state authority’s decision or failure to decide an application for a mining lease.
predicates.prior_central_order_unvaried: The central authority’s earlier order remained unvaried and unvacated.
predicates.later_review_reconsidered_prior_order: In a later review, the central authority reconsidered the matter decided by its earlier order.
predicates.fresh_ground_arose_after_prior_order: A material ground warranting reconsideration arose after the earlier order was made.

issues.definition: When a later review reconsiders an unvaried earlier order and no fresh material ground arose afterward, the central authority cannot reverse that order.
